Flowchart click href/tooltip node interactions (grouping G), implemented exactly as decided (bd show jmuir-dzd's own notes): href/tooltip form only. New DiagramNode.link (href/tooltip/target) model field + shared isAllowedLinkHref() scheme-allowlist check (http(s)/relative only). Parser: CLICK_HREF_DIRECTIVE parses the real form; CLICK_CALL_DIRECTIVE explicitly REJECTS 'click <id> call fn()' with a clean, named parse error (never silently dropped or executed) -- checked before href so no call variant can slip through as something else. An href with a disallowed scheme is also a hard parse error, not silent tolerance. Serializer re-emits a real 'click <id> href ...' line (native Mermaid grammar, not front-matter, matching subgraph direction's own precedent) -- applied as a second pass, and a node referencing an undeclared id is silently skipped (style directive's own established precedent, not an FR-003 violation). SVG export renderer wraps the node's shape+label in a real <a href> (with a <title> child for the tooltip), re-validating isAllowedLinkHref independently as defense in depth since link is also settable directly via diagram-ops.ts. New setNodeLink op (throws on a disallowed scheme, mirroring updateNodeLabel's own empty-label precedent) backs a new flowchart-only canvas UI popup (LinkPopup, opened via a new per-node Link affordance) that sets/clears href+tooltip+target, with client-side validation before ever calling the throwing op. Routed through appsec-expert review before merge per the bead's own explicit requirement given the disclosed XSS risk -- the FIRST pass came back 'DO NOT MERGE' with two real, live, verified bypasses: (1) isAllowedLinkHref's original hand-rolled regex missed a leading-whitespace/control-character scheme obfuscation (' javascript:...' matched no scheme prefix at all under the regex, so was wrongly treated as a safe relative path, while the WHATWG URL Standard every real browser implements strips that same leading whitespace before scheme detection -- fixed by delegating to the platform's own URL parser (new URL(href, base).protocol) instead of re-implementing its normalization by hand); (2) unescaped '"'/newline characters in href/tooltip could break out of the DSL's own unescapable '"..."' click-href token and inject a second, independent 'click <otherNodeId> href ...' line targeting an unrelated node whose own href was never validated -- fixed by rejecting (not escaping, since the DSL grammar has no escape syntax to produce) any href/tooltip containing a quote or line break, enforced at setNodeLink, defensively re-checked in serializeClickHref (which now treats a violation as 'no link' rather than ever emitting broken/injectable DSL), and in the canvas popup's own client-side validation. Also fixed, as recommended hardening: apps/api's export route now sends Content-Disposition: attachment (a fixed, non-diagram-derived filename, so the fix itself can't become a new header-injection surface) on all three export formats, since a direct GET with no download-forcing header would otherwise render the SVG inline at the API's own origin, widening any XSS-class bug's blast radius. The reviewer re-verified the fixed code independently (re-ran every original bypass payload against the corrected functions, ran the full diagram-core/apps/api suites themselves) and gave explicit sign-off to merge. Also fixed a small cosmetic gap the reviewer noted in passing: the parse-error message for a disallowed scheme now names the real scheme (reusing the same URL-parser resolution) instead of falling back to a generic '(unknown)' for an obfuscated href. New test coverage across every layer: flowchart-click-href.test.ts (29 tests: parse/serialize/round-trip, the call() rejection, the full scheme-allowlist including every bypass class, isAllowedLinkHref unit tests, and the serializer's own defensive-omission cases for a maliciously-direct model), render-svg.test.ts (10 new tests: <a>/<title> wrapping, target, XML-escaping including the literal double-quote/script-tag PoC, and the export-boundary re-check for both a plain and an obfuscated disallowed scheme), diagram-ops.test.ts (11 new tests for setNodeLink including the quote/newline rejection cases), apps/api diagrams.test.ts (Content-Disposition assertions on all 3 formats), and a new e2e spec (flowchart-click-link.spec.ts, 12 tests: affordance visibility per family, full set/edit/clear/reopen/Escape flows, and 3 dedicated client-side-rejection tests for the javascript:/data:/leading-space/quote-injection cases).
